context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform by introducing a hybrid cloud application. It enables incremental claim-type migration while ensuring zero data loss and maintaining legacy system-of-record operations.]

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Business Operations / Compliance Officers
- New Claims Platform (Azure West Europe)
- Legacy Mainframe (On-premise COBOL/DB2)
- Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD
- Payment Gateway (Third-party SaaS)
- Notification Service (Email/SMS provider)

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers -> New Claims Platform: HTTPS (Web/Mobile UI)
- Claims Adjusters -> New Claims Platform: HTTPS (Web App < 2s load time)
- New Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe: Asynchronous messaging via Azure Service Bus and ESB
- New Claims Platform -> Payment Gateway: HTTPS/REST (Claim settlements)
- New Claims Platform -> Notification Service: HTTPS/API (Customer alerts)
- New Claims Platform -> Insurer's Active Directory: OIDC/OAuth2 (Single Sign-On)

## Technology Stack
- Microsoft Azure West Europe: Cloud provider chosen for managed services and team enablement.
- Azure Landing Zones: Enforces security compliance to compensate for low cloud experience.
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event-driven messaging with outbox pattern for data consistency.
- Azure Monitor & OpenTelemetry: End-to-end distributed tracing and audit logging.
- GitHub Actions / Azure DevOps: CI/CD pipelines enabling the 1-day migration rollback requirement.

## Rationale
[The hybrid event-driven architecture insulates the modern Azure UI from legacy mainframe latencies to meet strict performance targets. Using managed Azure services bridges the team's cloud skill gap while guaranteeing financial consistency and rapid rollback capabilities.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform by introducing a hybrid cloud architecture. It gradually migrates claim types over three years while ensuring continuous legacy processing and zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer & Broker Portal (React SPA)
- Adjuster Web Application (React SPA)
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Fronend (Node.js/NestJS)
- Claims Core Processing Service (.NET Core / C# on Azure App Service)
- Mainframe Integration Adapter (Azure Functions / App Service)
- Azure Service Bus (Messaging & DLQ)
- Azure SQL Database
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 System of Record)
- Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers interact with Customer & Broker Portal via HTTPS/JSON
- Claims Adjusters interact with Adjuster Web Application via HTTPS/JSON
- Portals communicate with API Gateway / BFF via HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway communicates with Claims Core Processing Service and Mainframe Integration Adapter via gRPC/HTTPS
- Claims Core Processing Service publishes and consumes messages via Azure Service Bus using AMQP
- Mainframe Integration Adapter communicates with Legacy Mainframe using legacy protocols (MQ/CICS) respecting the 23:00-05:00 batch window pause
- Services authenticate against Azure Active Directory using OAuth2/OpenID Connect

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React hosted on Azure Static Web Apps
- Backend & BFF: Node.js/NestJS and .NET Core / C#
- Compute & Hosting: Azure App Service and Azure Functions (Managed PaaS)
- Database: Azure SQL Database
- Messaging: Azure Service Bus with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ)
- Identity & Security: Azure Active Directory via OAuth2/OpenID Connect
- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform / Bicep

## Rationale
The hybrid PaaS architecture minimizes cloud complexity for an inexperienced team while decoupling the UI from slow mainframe responses to meet performance goals. Standardizing on Azure Service Bus and managed Azure services ensures reliable event handling, strict batch-window isolation, and a smooth three-year migration path.

Customer & Broker Portal.analysis:
## Overview
Modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by replacing a 30-year-old mainframe via a gradual, hybrid cloud migration. Maintains system integrity and zero-downtime processing while migrating claim types one by one.

## Key Elements
* Customers & Brokers
* Claims Adjusters
* Customer & Broker Portal (React SPA / Azure Static Web Apps)
* Adjuster Web Application (React SPA / Azure Static Web Apps)
* API Gateway / BFF (Node.js / NestJS)
* Claims Core Processing Service (.NET Core / C# on Azure App Service)
* Mainframe Integration Adapter (Azure Functions / App Service)
* Azure Service Bus with DLQ
* Azure SQL Database
* Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (On-premises)
* Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD

## Relationships
* Customers & Brokers -> Customer & Broker Portal: Submits and manages claims [HTTPS/JSON]
* Customer & Broker Portal -> API Gateway / BFF: Communicates for data and operations [HTTPS/REST]
* Customer & Broker Portal -> Azure AD: Authenticates users [OAuth2/OpenID Connect]
* Customer & Broker Portal -> Azure Blob Storage: Uploads attachments directly [HTTPS/SAS Tokens]
* Adjuster Web Application -> API Gateway / BFF: Manages claims [HTTPS/REST]
* API Gateway / BFF -> Claims Core Processing Service: Invokes core logic [gRPC/HTTPS]
* Claims Core Processing Service -> Azure SQL Database: Persists state [T-SQL/TCP]
* Claims Core Processing Service -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes domain events [AMQP]
* Mainframe Integration Adapter -> Legacy COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Syncs legacy claims [Batch/MQ]

## Technology Stack
* Frontend: React SPA hosted on Azure Static Web Apps for rapid, cloud-simple delivery
* Backend API: Node.js with NestJS and .NET Core / C# for robust business logic
* Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus with Dead Letter Queues for reliable event streaming
* Database: Azure SQL Database for relational transactional storage
* Cloud Provider: Hybrid architecture spanning On-Premises Mainframe and Azure West Europe

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture balances strict legacy constraints with modern cloud capabilities by keeping the mainframe as the system of record while offloading new workloads to Azure. Using managed services like Azure Static Web Apps and Azure App Service minimizes operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.

Adjuster Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Adjuster Web Application modernizes the regional insurer's claims platform via a React single-page application hosted on Azure Static Web Apps. It interfaces with a Node.js API Gateway to process claims while safely coexisting with the legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe.

## Key Elements
- Claim Workspace Router & State Manager (React Context / Zustand)
- Claim Details View Component (React)
- Auth Guard Component (MSAL.js)
- Inline Audit & Exception Flagging Component (React with React Hook Form & Zod)
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (Node.js / NestJS)
- Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web Application: Interacts with web app via HTTPS/JSON
- Adjuster Web Application -> API Gateway / BFF: Communicates for data/operations via HTTPS/REST and WebSockets
- Adjuster Web Application -> Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD: Authenticates via OAuth2/OpenID Connect

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Chosen for responsive UI components and developer familiarity.
- Azure Static Web Apps: Selected for globally distributed, zero-downtime deployments.
- Zustand & React Context: Utilized for high-performance local UI state management and optimistic updates.
- MSAL.js: Implements secure Single Sign-On via OAuth2/OIDC.
- Zod & React Hook Form: Ensures rigorous client-side validation for exception reports.
- Azure Application Insights & Playwright: Mandated for synthetic monitoring and telemetry to guarantee sub-2s load times.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the responsive user interface from slow legacy backend responses using optimistic updates and caching. It ensures strict security, maintainability, and auditability during the hybrid migration phase.

API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture summary outlines the API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) for the Insurance Claims Modernization system. Its core purpose is to securely route, aggregate, and abstract hybrid traffic between modern web frontends and the legacy mainframe.

## Key Elements
- **Authentication & Authorization Component**: Passport.js and OIDC validator for Azure AD tokens.
- **Customer BFF Router & Aggregator**: NestJS controller handling lightweight customer and broker portals.
- **Adjuster BFF Router & Aggregator**: NestJS controller providing parallel data fetching and caching for claims adjusters.
- **Migration Routing Proxy**: NestJS middleware/interceptor dynamically routing claim types based on migration state.
- **API Composition & Data Shaping Service**: RxJS-based service managing parallel data aggregation and partial-response fallbacks.
- **Audit Logging & Analytics Component**: Interceptor emitting asynchronous telemetry to Azure Application Insights.

## Relationships
- Customer & Broker Portal -> Authentication & Authorization Component: Authenticates users [HTTPS/OAuth2/OIDC]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Authentication & Authorization Component: Authenticates users [HTTPS/OAuth2/OIDC]
- Customer BFF Router -> Claims Core Processing Service: Invokes core claims [gRPC/HTTPS]
- Adjuster BFF Router -> Mainframe Integration Adapter: Communicates with legacy backend [gRPC/HTTPS]
- Migration Routing Proxy -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes asynchronous events [AMQP]
- Audit Logging & Analytics Component -> Azure Application Insights: Dispatches telemetry [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js / NestJS**: Chosen as the runtime and framework for the BFF due to its modular architecture and TypeScript support.
- **RxJS**: Utilized for reactive programming, `forkJoin` parallel fetching, and error recovery (`catchError`).
- **gRPC**: Selected for high-performance, low-latency inter-service communication with internal microservices.
- **Azure Container Apps**: Hosting platform providing auto-scaling and traffic splitting for a team with low cloud experience.
- **Passport.js / OIDC**: Implements Single Sign-On integration with corporate Active Directory / Azure AD.

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces strict separation of concerns, tailoring payloads for distinct personas to meet aggressive performance targets. Furthermore, its built-in resilience patterns and dynamic routing abstract hybrid mainframe complexities, protecting data consistency during the migration.

Claims Core Processing Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native platform. It ensures zero claim loss and rapid adjuster response times during a phased, multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
- Claims Workflow Orchestrator (MassTransit State Machine)
- Claim Domain Model (.NET Core)
- Mainframe Sync Coordinator (.NET Core with Polly)
- Payout & Ledger Engine (.NET Core)
- Azure Container Apps (ACA)
- Azure Service Bus with DLQ
- Azure SQL Database

## Relationships
- Claims Workflow Orchestrator -> Claim Domain Model: Invokes [In-process]
- Claims Workflow Orchestrator -> Payout & Ledger Engine: Initiates disbursements [In-process]
- Claims Workflow Orchestrator -> Azure SQL Database: Persists state [Entity Framework Core / T-SQL]
- Claims Workflow Orchestrator -> Azure Service Bus: Dispatches domain events [AMQP]
- Mainframe Sync Coordinator -> Mainframe Integration Adapter: Syncs dual-writes [gRPC/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core / C#: Chosen for high performance and strong typing.
- Azure Container Apps (ACA) with KEDA: Simplifies event-driven scaling with low cloud experience.
- MassTransit: Manages sagas and state machines to guarantee consistency.
- Polly: Implements circuit breakers for resilient mainframe integration.
- Azure SQL Database: Provides reliable relational persistence and audit trails.
- Bicep: Manages Infrastructure as Code to prevent drift.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture uses event-driven microservices on Azure to decouple the modern web UI from slow mainframe latency. It guarantees strict consistency and rapid fallback capabilities required during the 3-year migration.

Mainframe Integration Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based platform while ensuring continuous legacy claims processing. It provides online claim submission for customers and a new web application for adjusters in a hybrid cloud deployment.]

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Mainframe Integration Adapter (Azure App Service container running .NET 8)
- Adapter API Controller (.NET 8 / Web API)
- Mainframe Broker Client (.NET 8 with Polly circuit breakers)
- Routing & Feature Flag Component (.NET 8)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 with IBM MQ/CICS)
- Azure App Configuration

## Relationships
- API Gateway/BFF -> Adapter API Controller: [gRPC/HTTPS]
- Mainframe Broker Client -> Legacy Mainframe: [IBM MQ / CICS over TLS]
- Routing Component -> Azure App Configuration: [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Containerized single deployment unit chosen to minimize operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.
- .NET 8 (C#): Core runtime for high-performance API handling and integration logic.
- IBM MQ / CICS: Enterprise messaging protocol for secure, reliable synchronization with the legacy mainframe.
- Azure App Configuration: Externalized config store enabling sub-one-day claim type rollback capability without code redeployments.
- Polly (.NET library): Provides automated circuit breakers to strictly respect the 23:00–05:00 mainframe batch window.
- OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing for end-to-end observability and zero data loss compliance.

## Rationale
[The architecture employs a streamlined Azure App Service container design to accommodate the team's limited cloud experience while strictly enforcing non-functional requirements. It guarantees zero data loss and sub-2-second adjuster response times through isolated integration components, strict batch-window protocols, and externalized feature flags.]

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system through a hybrid cloud platform using Azure services. Its core purpose is to gradually migrate claim types while ensuring data consistency and continuous legacy processing.]

## Key Elements
- Claims Core Processing Service (.NET Core / C# on Azure App Service)
- Mainframe Integration Adapter (Azure Functions / App Service)
- Azure Service Bus (Standard Tier with DLQ)
- `Claims.Events` Topic (AMQP 1.0)
- `Mainframe.Outbox` Queue (with FIFO sessions)
- Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) with DLQ Reprocessing Handler
- Azure SQL Database

## Relationships
- Claims Core Processing Service -> `Claims.Events`: Publishes domain events with W3C trace context [AMQP 1.0]
- Mainframe Integration Adapter -> `Mainframe.Outbox`: Consumes sync commands with FIFO ordering [AMQP 1.0]
- DLQ -> DLQ Reprocessing Handler: Forwards poisoned messages for administrative review [AMQP / Event Grid]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus: Chosen for reliable asynchronous messaging, topics, and DLQ support to meet consistency requirements (R-04) and enable quick rollbacks (R-06).
- Terraform / Bicep: Used for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to ensure repeatable, drift-free deployments given the team's low cloud experience.
- Azure Managed Identities: Enforces secure Azure RBAC instead of connection strings for enhanced security.
- Application Insights / Azure Monitor: Implements tracking, alerting, and metrics for DLQ and subscription lag.

## Rationale
[This architecture successfully decouples the modern cloud platform from the legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe using reliable asynchronous messaging and strict metadata tracking. It minimizes expensive mainframe changes while guaranteeing strict data consistency and low operational risk during the 3-year migration.]

Azure SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
- Hybrid insurance claims modernization platform replacing a 30-year-old mainframe.
- Azure SQL Database providing transactional persistence and synchronization for incrementally migrated claims.

## Key Elements
- Azure SQL Database (Managed relational data store in Azure West Europe)
- Claim Data Store (Extensible relational tables)
- Audit & Security Subsystem (Row-Level Security and Azure SQL Audit)
- Change Data Capture / CDC (Row-level change emitter)
- Partitioning & Retention Engine (Sliding window table partitioning)
- Read-Only Replica Routing (Secondary read endpoint)

## Relationships
- Claims Core Processing Service -> Azure SQL Database: Reads and writes claim data via T-SQL / TDS (TLS 1.3)
- Mainframe Integration Adapter -> Azure SQL Database: Synchronizes state via T-SQL / TDS Change Data Capture
- Reporting / Compliance Tools -> Azure SQL Database: Queries analytical data via Read-Only Replica T-SQL / TDS
- Partitioning Engine -> Azure Blob Storage: Archives historical claims via External Tables / Managed Backup

## Technology Stack
- Azure SQL Database: Fully managed service mitigating low team cloud experience
- Azure AD / Managed Identities: Secure passwordless authentication eliminating hardcoded connection strings
- Azure Blob Storage: Cost-effective tier for historical claim archiving
- Bicep / Terraform & Flyway: Infrastructure-as-Code and automated database migration pipelines ensuring rollback safety

## Rationale
- Managed Azure SQL features reduce operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience while ensuring rapid one-day rollbacks.
- Read replicas and partitioning protect critical performance constraints, maintaining sub-second UI loads and preserving the rigid nightly batch window.
